To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we introduce DreamerV, a world model-based reinforcement learning agent which is the first to reach human-level performance on Atari, and we demonstrate its applicability on continuous control tasks.
we introduce the first reinforcement learning agent that achieves human level performance on the Atari 55 games benchmark purely by learning behaviors in a separately trained world-model.

(1) we introduce a new agent, DreamerV2 that achieves human-level Atari performance by learning behaviors from predictions inside a separately trained discrete world model; (2) DreamerV2 surpasses the previous state-of-the-art on the Atari benchmark with the same computational and wall-clock time budget; (3) DreamerV 2 is applicable to tasks with continous actions, where it solves stand-up and walk from pixel inputs
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: how much information is necessary to solve complex tasks?
the question of whether we can learn a compact world model and derive successful behaviors purely from its predictions.
the question of what is the most efficient way to learn behaviors from pixel inputs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DreamerV2 learns behaviors purely from the predictions of a world model, which is trained separately from behavior learning.
Dreamer V2 is the first model that achieves human-level Atari performance by learning behaviors inside an accurate world model.
DreamerV2 learns behaviors purely from world-model predictions and surpasses state-of-the-art performance in the Atari benchmark and continuous control tasks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DreamerV2 can learn a discrete representation for the world model that can be used to train a policy for the Atari game.
we show how the latent space of a world model can be used as a compact representation for the agent to learn behaviors.
Dreamer V2 achieves human-level performance in 55 Atari environments by learning behaviors purely from predictions of a separately trained, compact world model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
learning behaviors inside the latent space of a world model, trained separately from a policy, is a promising approach for general-purpose reinforcement learning agents.
a world model that is learned separately from a policy can be used to learn behaviors that are competitive with state-of-the-art agents.
learning behaviors purely from a world model is possible for a wide range of complex environments, including Atari games, and even for tasks with continuous action spaces.
